title: TURN YOUR SERVICE INTO AN OFFER WITH CHATGPT
content:
A service becomes easier to understand when the customer can tell what they are buying. This guide turns the direction from the previous step into a defined offer.

The goal is not clever naming. It is clarity.

WHAT AN OFFER NEEDS TO ANSWER
Who is it for? What problem or task does it address? What exactly will you do? What is included and excluded? What does the customer receive? How long does it take? What does the customer need to provide? Is it one-time or recurring?

SCOPE PROTECTS BOTH SIDES
A vague promise such as "unlimited help with your business" can create mismatched expectations. A defined scope makes it easier for the customer to judge fit and easier for you to estimate workload.

DO NOT PROMISE RESULTS YOU CANNOT CONTROL
You can promise the work you will perform and the deliverables you will provide. Be careful about guaranteeing outcomes that depend on customers, markets, platforms, health, legal decisions, or other factors outside your control.

HOW TO USE THIS
Paste the prompt below after you have a reasonably specific service direction.

COPY & PASTE INTO CHATGPT

During the interview:
- Ask one question at a time unless closely related questions are easier together.
- Use my answers before deciding what to ask next.
- If I do not know, help me identify the decision rather than filling it in silently.
- Keep the offer within my actual skills and capacity.
- Flag legal, licensing, insurance, tax, or regulated requirements for independent verification when relevant.

Help me turn my service direction into a clear offer. Interview me about the intended customer, the task or problem, what I will actually do, deliverables, scope boundaries, customer responsibilities, timeline, communication, revisions if relevant, whether the work is one-time or recurring, and how much direct time delivery requires.

Help me define the smallest useful version I could responsibly sell. Do not create guarantees for outcomes outside my control. Do not invent market pricing or legal requirements. If pricing comes up, help me identify cost, time, capacity, and market information I would need before setting it.

At the end give me:
- Offer name or plain-language label
- Intended customer
- Problem/task
- What is included
- What is not included
- Deliverables
- Delivery process
- Expected direct time per customer
- One-time or recurring structure
- Assumptions and external facts to verify
- A concise description I could use to explain the offer

WHERE TO GO NEXT
Continue to PDF 45 if you want to examine how dependent the service is on your time. If the offer is already a fit and you are comfortable with its capacity, continue to PDF 46.
